LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: OPEN ENDED COMPOSITIONS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions, part of Strand 2 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How do we express ideas on different topics? 2. Why do we share ideas?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm possible points to include in their composition,

2. write the first paragraph with peers while observing correct punctuation and spelling,

3. complete the composition of about (100-150 words),

4. work jointly to proofread their compositions,

5. display the completed compositions in class,

6. conduct a gallery walk and give feedback,

7. search and read compositions online. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm possible points to include in their composition,
2. write the first paragraph with peers while observing correct punctuation and spelling,
3. complete the composition of about (100-150 words),
4. work jointly to proofread their compositions,
5. display the completed compositions in class,
6. conduct a gallery walk and give feedback,
7. search and read compositions online. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing: Open ended Compositions together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn is promoted as the learner reflects on their learning as they work collaboratively with peers to

proofread compositions.

• Critical Thinking and problem solving is advanced as the learner brainstorms on possible points to use when

writing compositions and when they complete the composition.

Values:
Responsibility is enhanced as the learner offers leadership and guidance to others as they collaborate to plan and create

compositions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skill Education is achieved as the learner expresses ideas effectively during discussion and in writing composition.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner applies the skill of composition writing when learning other subject like Kiswahili.
